status: frozen 2026-10-06: 12 families; fit authorized (J-10); any change is chicago_model_v2

conventions.C2: density denominator = Community Area land: area minus municipal hydrography (Hydro_20260916), release field hydro_land_m2; decided 2026-10-02
conventions.C3: each family lists source, release, observation period and SHA-256; vintages are disclosed, not aligned

families.name: resident density
families.definition: ACS 2020-2024 5-year B01003 total population allocated to the Community Area / land km2
families.allocation: block-group estimate -> its 2020 blocks by 2020 POP20 share -> Community Area by block land share (S1-3, S1-7a)
families.uncertainty: 90% MOE = sqrt(sum((weight x block-group MOE)^2)); understates (no covariance)
stated_limits: population pooled over 2020-2024, not a 2024 count; 2020 distribution assumed inside each block group
margins of error understate uncertainty (no covariance between block groups)
Burnside (CHI:47, CV 16.8%) and Fuller Park (CHI:37, CV 14.2%) exceed the 12% CV gate; accepted because each 90% interval spans 3 rank positions among the lowest-density areas
O'Hare (CHI:76): block-group land split would add 9.5%; 2020-block split kept because the land split assigns residents to airport land
land includes parks, vacant land, cemeteries and the airport (C2): redundancy with U1 and other densities to be checked at the final joint review
municipal hydrography covers the city only

families.name: public transport accessibility (PTAL Access Index)
families.definition: resident-weighted mean over 100 m grid locations of the TfL PTAL Access Index, weekday 08:15-09:15, Wednesday 2026-10-14; modes CTA bus, CTA 'L' (metro), Metra (rail)
families.method: TfL Connectivity Assessment Guide 2015, section 2, applied unchanged: walk 4.8 km/h on Overture segments without motorway/trunk (footways included); max walk 640 m bus, 960 m metro/rail; AWT = 0.5*60/f + reliability (2 bus, 0.75 metro/rail); EDF = 30/TAT; nearest stop per route, most frequent direction; per mode best EDF + 0.5*others; rail services need >= 2 city stops
families.observation_period: scheduled service on 2026-10-14 (CTA feed Sept 2026; Metra feed saved 2026-10-05)
stated_limits: service near home, not where it goes
grows with the number of routes faster than with one route's frequency (cross-city levels need a decision at the common stage)
scheduled service, not reliability; Pace suburban buses excluded (EMTU excluded in Sao Paulo for symmetry)

footway sensitivity: streets-only network lowers values by a median 3.7%; Near South Side, Douglas and Archer Heights change by more than 10% (Archer Heights 6 ranks); footways kept because they carry real links
walking network ignores slope, crossings and safety; points snapped to the nearest network node
Metra Heritage Corridor has no departure counted in the window
families.sao_paulo_values: same table, city == 'SP', kept for the common-model stage (Census 2022 tract residents; SPTrans bus, Metro, CPTM)

families.name: registered workplace-job density

families.source: LODES 8 WAC 2023, S000 JT00 (unemployment-insurance-covered and Federal jobs, all jobs per person, about 1 April 2023)
families.allocation: 2020 block -> Community Area by land share (same rule as U3)
stated_limits: registered jobs at the employer's establishment, not where people physically work; self-employed and informal work excluded
location error unmeasured in Chicago (no area-level independent source; CMAP 2024-25 survey has a median of 6 workers per community area)
Woodlawn (-5.4%, 5 ranks) and Hegewisch (-23.6%) change under the CMAP business-land allocation; land share kept for consistency with U3
LODES is partially synthetic with disclosure protection
Loop, Hyde Park and O'Hare change by more than 10% without the 10 largest job blocks
reference date about 1 April 2023 (Sao Paulo RAIS: 2022 reference year)

stated_limits: mapped footprint coverage, not surveyed coverage

Overture release 2026; observation dates of individual footprints are not uniform

Limit: 22 districts whose Overture footprints are more than 50% machine-learning-derived (North, South, West) are a median 13.4% below the 2007-2014 municipal GeoSampa map and rank on average 10 places lower; per-district flag in analysis/results/SP_CHI/b1_step4_2026_10_05/tables/b1_sp_explanations.csv (ml_share)

families.name: vertical form (built-surface-weighted height)
families.definition: GHSL R2023A built-surface-weighted building height on land: sum(volume) / sum(built surface) over native 100 m cells weighted by cell-land overlap
families.source: GHSL GHS-BUILT-H ANBH/AGBH epoch 2018 and GHS-BUILT-V 2020, 100 m, Mollweide
families.replaces: frozen land-weighted ANBH mean including empty cells (mixed coverage and height)
families.bi_decision: no separate BI family: BI equals BV x GHSL built fraction (Spearman 0.9999); BI reported descriptively as bi_volume_per_land_m
stated_limits: modeled height (GHSL epoch 2018, 100 m cells), not measured
Spearman 0.852 with Cook 2022 LiDAR building height; GHSL a median 5% lower
tall areas compressed: areas with LiDAR height >= 25 m read at 0.59 of LiDAR (Loop 42 m)

absolute levels compared across cities under C6: against LiDAR with the same method, GHSL is about 10-15% higher relative to LiDAR in Sao Paulo than in Chicago within each height class (corrected 2026-10-06; the earlier 1.6-2x reading relied on references that understate height)

grade separation ignored (bridges split land beneath)

families.definition: share of classified occupied lot land in residential, industrial and institutional use (commerce is the remainder and failed admission)

admission.rule: max |Spearman| with U6 coordinates, B1 and M1 < 0.70 in both cities (pre-registered 2026-10-06)

families.missing_rule: S7-4 extended to the shares: missing where classified occupied land < 10% of land (O'Hare, 4.9%); J-8 available-case distance

primary use per lot; observed (CMAP) vs declared (IPTU) use across cities

model.output: 77 x 77 dissimilarity matrix; each area's five nearest neighbours with family contributions (J-1)
model.transforms: log: U2, U3, U4, M1, M7, BV height, M4 elongation; identity: B1, M6, M4 compactness, M3 (already ln), U6, U1 (J-5)
model.scaling: z-score with population SD on the 77 areas, capped at +-3; U6 log-ratios unscaled (J-6)
model.budgets: equal per family (12 families); U6 = 1/2 intensity + 1/2 Aitchison composition; within a family, mean of squared column differences (J-7)
model.calibration: each block divided by its median positive pairwise mean squared difference
model.distance: D^2 = sum over blocks of budget x share x calibrated block; pairs missing a family use the families both areas have, renormalized (J-8)
model.redundancy: J-4: no family pair with |Spearman| >= 0.90 in Chicago; no budgets merged

runs.R2_pca_weights: principal components of R1 (from D; equals PCA of the embedding when complete), fewest components reaching 90% variance, unwhitened
runs.R3_without_correlated_features: drop scalar columns while any pair has |Spearman| >= 0.70 (most pairs first; ties: higher mean |rho|, then later position); equal budgets over surviving families

model.sensitivities: leave-one-family-out; equal domain budgets; 500 weight draws x U(0.5,1.5) seed 20261006; robust IQR and rank-normal scaling; Ledoit-Wolf Mahalanobis; M3 unweighted, M7 median parcel size, BV volume, U6 confidence >= 0.3 (J-9)
model.stability_rule: a neighbour is stable if it stays in the area's top five in >= 80% of weight draws
